about: The Third Branch opens in London, where the seven survivors of the Irish war have buried the head of Bendigeidfran in the White Hill, and Manawydan son of Llŷr, whose cousin Caswallon son of Beli now wears the crown, looks about him and finds that he alone has nowhere to go. Pryderi gives him his mother Rhiannon as wife, with the enjoyment of the seven cantrefs of Dyfed, and at the feast in Arberth Manawydan and Rhiannon take to one another. When Pryderi has carried his homage to Caswallon, the four of them — Manawydan, Pryderi, Rhiannon and Cigfa — are sitting on the Mound of Arberth when a great noise and a shower of mist come down, and when it lifts Dyfed is empty of house, beast, smoke and man, and only the court stands, deserted. They live two years on game, fish and wild honey, then go into England to earn their keep: as saddlers at Hereford, as shield-makers in another town, as shoemakers in a third; each time Manawydan's work is so good that the craftsmen of the place plot to kill them. Each time Pryderi wants to fall on the churls, and each time Manawydan will not, and at the last he turns them back towards Dyfed.

sentences.t: Guedy daruot y'r seithwyr a dywedyssam ni uchot cladu penn Bendigeiduran yn y Gwynuryn yn Llundein, a'y wyneb ar Freinc, edrych a wnaeth Manauydan ar y dref yn Llundein, ac ar y gedymdeithon, a dodi ucheneit uawr, a chymryt diruawr alar a hiraeth yndaw.
sentences.l: After finishing for-the seven-men that we-said above burying the head of-Bendigeidfran in the White-Hill in London, and its face towards France, looking he-did Manawydan at the town in London, and at his companions, and putting a great sigh, and taking huge grief and longing in-him.
sentences.i: When the seven men of whom we spoke above had finished burying the head of Bendigeidfran in the White Hill in London, with its face towards France, Manawydan looked at the town of London, and at his companions, and heaved a great sigh, and great grief and longing took hold of him.
sentences.n: The Third Branch, Manawydan, begins here; the manuscript opens it with a large initial G. Guedy daruot y'r seithwyr … cladu 'after finishing to the seven men … burying': daruot 'come to pass, come to an end' takes y 'to' for the doer, the usual way of saying 'when they had finished'. seithwyr 'seven men' (seith + gwyr, g lost in the compound). a dywedyssam ni uchot 'that we said above': dywedyssam is the 1 pl. preterite of dywedut; the narrator's 'we' points back to the end of the Second Branch. Bendigeiduran is Bendigeit + Bran, b softened to u (= f). edrych a wnaeth Manauydan 'looking did Manawydan' = Manawydan looked: the verbal noun, then a wnaeth, then the subject — the tale's great narrative pattern; the verbal nouns that follow (a dodi, a chymryt, spirant after a) carry on under it. Manauydan is spelt with u only here; everywhere else in the part it is Manawydan. Old spellings to expect throughout: u for v/f, k for c, final -t for -d, d for dd. y dref ← tref after the feminine article; y gedymdeithon ← kedymdeithon after y 'his'; ucheneit uawr, mawr softened after a feminine noun; diruawr 'huge' stands before its noun and softens it (alar ← galar). yndaw 'in him' is yn conjugated, 3 sg. masc.

sentences.t: “Oy a Duw holl gyuoethawc, guae ui,” heb ef, “nyt oes neb heb le idaw heno namyn mi.”
sentences.l: “Oh God all-powerful, woe to-me,” said he, “there-is-not anyone without place to-him tonight but me.”
sentences.i: “Oh God almighty, woe is me,” he said, “there is no one but me without a place to go tonight.”
sentences.n: Oy a Duw 'Oh God' (house rendering), with holl gyuoethawc 'all-powerful' ← kyuoethawc 'mighty, rich', softened after holl. guae ui 'woe to me': ui is mi softened (u = f). nyt oes neb 'there is not anyone'. heb le ← lle, softened after heb 'without'. idaw 'to him', y 'to' conjugated. namyn 'except, but'. heb ef 'said he': heb is the verb used only to tag speech.

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb y Pryderi, “na uit kyn drymhet genhyt a hynny. Dy geuynderw yssyd urenhin yn Ynys y Kedyrn; a chyn gwnel gameu it,” heb ef, “ny buost hawlwr tir a dayar eiryoet. Trydyd lledyf unben wyt.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said Pryderi, “let-it-not-be so heavy with-you as that. Your cousin it-is-who-is king in the Island of-the Mighty; and though he-do wrongs to-you,” said he, “you-were-not a claimer of-land and ground ever. Third yielding chieftain you-are.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” said Pryderi, “do not take it so heavily. Your cousin is king in the Island of the Mighty; and though he may do you wrong,” he said, “you were never a claimant of land and territory. You are the third Yielding Chieftain.”
sentences.n: heb y Pryderi 'said Pryderi': before a named speaker heb takes y. na uit 'let it not be': bit, the 3 sg. imperative of bot, softened after the negative na. kyn drymhet … a hynny 'as heavy as that': the equative of trwm (trymhet), softened after kyn 'so'. genhyt 'with you' (gan, 2 sg.). Dy geuynderw ← keuynderw 'first cousin', softened after dy. yssyd 'who is', the relative form of bot; urenhin ← brenhin softened after it. a chyn gwnel 'and though he do': kyn 'though' with the present subjunctive of gwneuthur. ny buost 'you were not', 2 sg. preterite of bot. hawlwr 'claimant' (hawl 'claim' + gwr). Trydyd lledyf unben refers to a triad of 'Three ... Chieftains' in which Manawydan is named; lledyf means 'slanting, soft, meek, humble', and what kind of chieftain is meant — yielding, unassuming, landless — is disputed; the context (he never claimed land) is the best guide, and 'Yielding' is only a choice. unben 'chieftain' (house).

sentences.t: “Ie,” heb ef, “kyt boet keuynderw y mi y gwr hwnnw, goathrist yw genhyf i guelet neb yn lle Bendigeiduran uy mrawt, ac ny allaf uot yn llawen yn un ty ac ef.”
sentences.l: “Yes,” said he, “though be cousin to me that man, somewhat-sad it-is with-me to see anyone in the place of-Bendigeidfran my brother, and I-cannot be glad in one house with him.”
sentences.i: “Yes,” he said, “though that man is my cousin, it grieves me sorely to see anyone in the place of Bendigeidfran my brother, and I cannot be glad under one roof with him.”
sentences.n: Ie 'Yes' (house). kyt boet 'though it be': kyt (kyn before a vowel) with boet, the subjunctive of bot. y mi 'to me'. goathrist yw genhyf 'it is goathrist with me': athrist is 'very sad' (intensive a- + trist), and go- usually means 'somewhat, rather'; whether the compound is a dry understatement ('rather sad') or simply 'grievous' is uncertain, and i takes it as strong. guelet is gwelet 'see' written gu-. uy mrawt 'my brother': brawt with nasal mutation after uy. ny allaf ← gallaf softened after ny; uot ← bot softened after it. yn un ty ac ef 'in one house with him'.

sentences.t: “A wney ditheu gynghor arall?” heb y Pryderi.
sentences.l: “Will-you-do you-for-your-part another counsel?” said Pryderi.
sentences.i: “Will you take other counsel, then?” said Pryderi.
sentences.n: A wney: the question particle a, which softens, with gwney, 2 sg. present of gwneuthur 'do'. ditheu ← titheu 'you for your part', softened after the verb. gynghor ← kynghor 'counsel', softened as the object.

sentences.t: “Reit oed im wrth gynghor,” heb ef, “a pha gynghor yw hwnnw?”
sentences.l: “Need was to-me of counsel,” said he, “and what counsel is that?”
sentences.i: “I could do with counsel,” he said, “and what counsel is it?”
sentences.n: Reit oed im wrth 'need was to me for' = I should need, I could do with: reit 'need', and the imperfect oed with a conditional sense. wrth 'for' softens: gynghor ← kynghor. a pha ← pa, spirant after a 'and'.

sentences.t: “Seith cantref Dyuet yr edewit y mi,” heb y Pryderi, “a Riannon uy mam yssyd yno. Mi a rodaf it honno, a medyant y seith cantref genthi.
sentences.l: “Seven cantrefs of-Dyfed it-is-that were-left to me,” said Pryderi, “and Rhiannon my mother it-is-who-is there. I it-is-that will-give to-you her, and the possession of-the seven cantrefs with-her.
sentences.i: “The seven cantrefs of Dyfed were left to me,” said Pryderi, “and Rhiannon my mother is there. I will give her to you, and the rule of the seven cantrefs with her.
sentences.n: Seith cantref Dyuet yr edewit y mi 'seven cantrefs of Dyfed were left to me': the subject stands first and the particle y (yr before a vowel) links it to the verb; edewit is the impersonal preterite of adaw 'leave'. Mi a rodaf 'I will give': the abnormal sentence, pronoun + a + verb, with nothing in particular stressed; rodaf is the 1 sg. present (with future sense) of rodi. it 'to you'. honno 'that one' (feminine), Rhiannon. medyant 'possession, dominion'. genthi 'with her' (gan, 3 sg. fem.).

sentences.t: A chyny bei itti o gyuoeth namyn y seith cantref hynny, nyt oes seith cantref well noc wy. Kicua uerch Wyn Gloyw yw uy gwreic inheu,” heb ef.
sentences.l: And though-not there-were to-you of realm but those seven cantrefs, there-is-not seven cantrefs better than they. Cigfa daughter of-Gwyn Gloyw is my wife for-my-part,” said he.
sentences.i: And though you had no realm but those seven cantrefs, there are no seven cantrefs better. Cigfa daughter of Gwyn Gloyw is my own wife,” he said.
sentences.n: A chyny 'and though not': kyny is kyn 'though' + ny 'not', with the spirant after a. bei 'there were', imperfect subjunctive of bot; itti 'to you', the fuller form of it. o gyuoeth 'of realm' ← kyuoeth, softened after o. well ← gwell 'better', softened, as it regularly is after nyt oes … ; noc wy 'than they' (noc before a vowel). Kicua is Cigfa (k = c, u = f); uerch ← merch after a name; Wyn ← Gwyn softened after uerch. In the First Branch (part 004) her father is Gwyn Gohoyw son of Gloyw Wallt Lydan; here the White Book calls him Gwyn Gloyw. yw 'is', with the predicate first. inheu 'I for my part' leans on uy: 'my own wife' — Pryderi has his wife, as Manawydan is to have his.

sentences.t: “A chyn bo enwedigaeth y kyuoeth y mi, bit y mwynant y ti a Riannon. A phei mynhut gyuoeth eiryoet, aduyd y caffut ti hwnnw.”
sentences.l: “And though be the ownership of-the realm to me, let-be the enjoyment to you and Rhiannon. And if you-wanted a realm ever, perhaps you-would-get you that.”
sentences.i: “And though the title to the realm be mine, let the enjoyment of it be yours and Rhiannon's. And if ever you had wanted a realm, perhaps you would have had that one.”
sentences.n: kyn bo 'though it be', bo the present subjunctive of bot. enwedigaeth 'specialness, particular ownership', the title as against mwynant 'enjoyment, use'. bit 'let it be', 3 sg. imperative of bot. A phei 'and if' (pei with the spirant after a) takes the imperfect subjunctive: mynhut 'you wanted' (mynnu), caffut 'you would get' (caffael). gyuoeth ← kyuoeth, softened as the object. aduyd: the White Book writes it as one word (Evans prints ad uyd), the Red Book atuyd. It seems to be an adverb 'perhaps, it may be', but its sense here is uncertain, and so is the sentence's point. The second witness supplies [waeth] 'worse' — 'perhaps you would get a worse one than that' — but the Red Book has no such word ('atuyd y kaffut ti hwnnw'), so nothing is supplied here; hwnnw 'that one' is taken to be the realm just offered.

sentences.t: “Na uynhaf, unben,” heb ef, “Duw a dalo it dy gydymdeithas.”
sentences.l: “I-do-not-want, chieftain,” said he, “God may-he-repay to-you your fellowship.”
sentences.i: “I do not want it, chieftain,” he said; “may God repay you your fellowship.”
sentences.n: Na uynhaf 'I do not want': Welsh answers by repeating the verb, here negated with na; uynhaf ← mynhaf, 1 sg. present of mynnu, softened. unben 'chieftain' (house). Duw a dalo it 'may God repay you' (house): talo, present subjunctive of talu, softened after a. dy gydymdeithas ← kydymdeithas, softened after dy; the same word as kedymdeithas 'fellowship', spelt with y. He refuses the realm and takes the friendship.

sentences.t: “E gedymdeithas oreu a allwyf i, y ti y byd, os mynny.”
sentences.l: “The fellowship best that I-may-be-able, to you it-will-be, if you-want.”
sentences.i: “The best fellowship I can give shall be yours, if you will have it.”
sentences.n: E is the article y, spelt e. gedymdeithas ← kedymdeithas, softened after the article (it is feminine), and so oreu ← goreu 'best' after it. a allwyf 'that I may be able': allwyf ← gallwyf, 1 sg. present subjunctive of gallu, softened after a. y ti y byd 'to you it will be': the phrase put first, then the particle y and byd, the future of bot. os mynny 'if you want': mynny, 2 sg. present of mynnu.

sentences.t: “Mynnaf, eneit,” heb ef, “Duw a dalo it. A mi a af gyt a thi y edrych Riannon, ac y edrych y kyuoeth.”
sentences.l: “I-want, soul,” said he, “God may-he-repay to-you. And I it-is-that will-go with you to see Rhiannon, and to see the realm.”
sentences.i: “I will, friend,” he said; “may God repay you. And I will go with you to see Rhiannon, and to see the realm.”
sentences.n: Mynnaf 'I want', the answer by the verb, positive this time. eneit 'soul', a warm address, 'friend'. mi a af 'I will go': af, 1 sg. present of mynet. gyt a thi 'with you': gyt a 'together with', and ti takes the spirant after a. y edrych 'to see': y 'to' + the verbal noun.

sentences.t: “Iawn a wney,” heb ynteu.
sentences.l: “Right it-is-that you-do,” said he-for-his-part.
sentences.i: “You do right,” he said.
sentences.n: Iawn a wney 'right (it is that) you do': the word that matters put first, then a and the verb (gwney, softened). heb ynteu 'said he', ynteu 'he for his part': Pryderi answering.

sentences.t: “Mi a debygaf na werendeweist eiryoet ar ymdidanwreic well no hi. Er amser y bu hitheu yn y dewred, ny bu wreic delediwach no hi, ac etwa ny bydy anuodlawn y phryt.”
sentences.l: “I it-is-that think that you-have-not-listened ever to a talk-woman better than she. Since the time that she-was in her prime, there-was-not a woman fairer than she, and still you-will-not-be displeased her form.”
sentences.i: “I think you never listened to a woman better to talk with than she. In the days when she was in her prime there was no woman lovelier, and even now you will not be displeased with her looks.”
sentences.n: Mi a debygaf 'I think': tebygaf, softened after a. na werendeweist 'that you did not listen': gwerendeweist, 2 sg. preterite of gwarandaw, softened after the negative na; ar 'to'. ymdidanwreic 'conversation-woman' (ymdidan 'talk' + gwreic), a woman to talk with. well ← gwell, softened after the feminine noun; no hi 'than she'. Er amser 'since the time, from the time'. yn y dewred 'in her prime': dewred seems to mean 'vigour, prime', but the word is rare and its sense not certain. wreic ← gwreic after ny bu; delediwach ← telediwach, comparative of telediw 'comely', softened after the feminine noun. etwa 'still, even now'. ny bydy, 2 sg. future of bot. anuodlawn y phryt 'displeased (with) her form': pryt with the spirant after y 'her'; no preposition is written.

sentences.t: Vynt a gerdassant racdunt.
sentences.l: They it-was-that walked before-them.
sentences.i: They went on their way.
sentences.n: Vynt is wynt 'they', written with V for w at the head of the paragraph. a gerdassant ← kerdassant, 3 pl. preterite of kerdet 'walk, go', softened after a: the abnormal sentence again. racdunt 'before them', i.e. onward: rac conjugated, 3 pl.

sentences.t: A pha hyt bynnac y bydynt ar y ford, wynt a doethant y Dyuet.
sentences.l: And whatever length they-were on the way, they it-was-that came to Dyfed.
sentences.i: And however long they were on the road, they came to Dyfed.
sentences.n: The formula of the journey to London at the end of the last branch. A pha hyt bynnac 'and whatever length': pa with the spirant after a, hyt 'length', bynnac '-ever'. y bydynt 'they were', the habitual past of bot. ford is ffordd 'way, road', f for ff. wynt a doethant 'they came': doethant, 3 pl. preterite of dyuot.

sentences.t: Gwled darparedic oed udunt erbyn eu dyuot yn Arberth, a Riannon a Chicua wedy y harlwyaw.
sentences.l: A feast prepared was for-them against their coming in Arberth, and Rhiannon and Cigfa after its preparing.
sentences.i: A feast was ready for them against their coming to Arberth, which Rhiannon and Cigfa had prepared.
sentences.n: darparedic 'prepared', a past participle in -edic (darparu). udunt 'for them' (y 'to', 3 pl.). erbyn 'against', by the time of. a Chicua: Kicua with the spirant after a. wedy y harlwyaw 'after its preparing' = having prepared it: the object of a verbal noun is a possessive before it, and y 'its' (for the feminine gwled) puts h before a vowel — arlwyaw 'prepare, lay out'.

sentences.t: Ac yna dechreu kydeisted ac ymdidan o Uanawydan a Riannon; ac o'r ymdidan tirioni a wnaeth y uryt a'y uedwl wrthi, a hoffi yn y uedwl na welsei eiryoed wreic digonach y theket a'y thelediwet no hi.
sentences.l: And then beginning sitting-together and talking by Manawydan and Rhiannon; and from the talk growing-tender did his mind and his thought towards-her, and liking in his thought that he-had-not-seen ever a woman more-complete her beauty and her comeliness than she.
sentences.i: And then Manawydan and Rhiannon began to sit together and talk; and from the talk his mind and his thought grew tender towards her, and it pleased him to think that he had never seen a woman more perfect in beauty and in grace than she.
sentences.n: dechreu kydeisted ac ymdidan o Uanawydan a Riannon 'beginning sitting together and talking by Manawydan and Rhiannon': o marks the doers of a verbal noun, and softens Manawydan. kydeisted 'sit together' (kyd- 'co-' + eisted). tirioni a wnaeth y uryt a'y uedwl 'growing kind did his mind and his thought': tirioni 'become gentle' (tirion), with the subject after a wnaeth; y uryt ← bryt, y uedwl ← medwl, softened after y 'his'. wrthi 'towards her' (wrth, 3 sg. fem.). hoffi 'take pleasure'. na welsei 'that he had not seen': gwelsei, the pluperfect, softened after na. eiryoed is spelt here with d, beside eiryoet elsewhere. digonach, comparative of digawn 'sufficient', 'more complete'. y theket a'y thelediwet 'her beauty and her comeliness': teket and telediwet with the spirant after y 'her'.

sentences.t: “Pryderi,” heb ef, “mi a uydaf wrth a dywedeisti.”
sentences.l: “Pryderi,” said he, “I it-is-that will-be by what you-said.”
sentences.i: “Pryderi,” he said, “I will abide by what you said.”
sentences.n: mi a uydaf 'I will be': bydaf, future of bot, softened after a. wrth 'by, according to'. a dywedeisti 'what you said': a 'that which', and dywedeisti is dywedeist (2 sg. preterite of dywedut) with ti fused on.

sentences.t: “Pa dywedwydat oed hwnnw?” heb y Riannon.
sentences.l: “What saying was that?” said Rhiannon.
sentences.i: “What saying was that?” said Rhiannon.
sentences.n: Pa dywedwydat: the form is odd, and its sense uncertain. It looks like a noun from dywedut 'say' (perhaps 'what was said, a saying'); Rhiannon, not having been party to the gift, asks what the word was. Taken here as 'what saying'. hwnnw 'that' (masculine).

sentences.t: “Arglwydes,” heb ef Pryderi, “mi a'th roessum yn wreic y Uanawydan uab Llyr.”
sentences.l: “Lady,” said he Pryderi, “I it-is-that gave you as wife to Manawydan son of-Llŷr.”
sentences.i: “Lady,” said Pryderi, “I have given you as wife to Manawydan son of Llŷr.”
sentences.n: Arglwydes 'Lady'. heb ef Pryderi 'said he, Pryderi': pronoun and name together, an unusual tag. mi a'th roessum 'I gave you': 'th is the infixed object pronoun 'you'; roessum is a 1 sg. preterite of rodi 'give', from its stem ro-. yn wreic 'as wife' ← gwreic, softened after predicative yn. y Uanawydan 'to Manawydan', softened after y 'to'; uab ← mab after the name.

sentences.t: “A minheu a uydef wrth hynny yn llawen,” heb y Riannon.
sentences.l: “And I-for-my-part it-is-that will-be by that gladly,” said Rhiannon.
sentences.i: “And I will abide by it gladly,” said Rhiannon.
sentences.n: a uydef: so the White Book (Evans auydef, plain on the page); it is a scribal slip for a uydaf 'I will be', the reading of the Red Book and of Manawydan's mi a uydaf just above, and is kept as written and read as uydaf. minheu 'I for my part', the pronoun answering Manawydan's. wrth hynny 'by that'. yn llawen 'gladly', the adverbial yn.

sentences.t: “Llawen yw genhyf inheu,” heb y Manawydan, “a Duw a dalo y'r gwr yssyd yn rodi i minheu y gedymdeithas mor difleis a hynny.”
sentences.l: “Glad it-is with-me for-my-part,” said Manawydan, “and God may-he-repay to the man who-is giving to me-for-my-part his fellowship as guileless as that.”
sentences.i: “I am glad of it too,” said Manawydan, “and may God repay the man who gives me his fellowship so frankly.”
sentences.n: Llawen yw genhyf 'glad it is with me' = I am glad: the predicate first. inheu 'I for my part', i minheu 'to me for my part'. heb y Manawydan, spelt with w as everywhere but the first unit. y'r gwr yssyd yn rodi 'to the man who is giving': y'r is y 'to' + yr 'the'. y gedymdeithas ← kedymdeithas, softened after y 'his'. mor difleis a hynny 'as difleis as that': mor softens, but d shows nothing. difleis seems to be 'without guile, sincere' (di- 'without'); the sense is from context.

sentences.t: Kyn daruot y wled honno, y kyscwyt genti.
sentences.l: Before finishing that feast, it-was-slept with-her.
sentences.i: Before that feast was over, he slept with her.
sentences.n: Kyn daruot 'before finishing', kyn 'before' with the verbal noun. y wled ← gwled after the feminine article; honno 'that' (fem.). y kyscwyt genti 'there was sleeping with her': kyscwyt is the impersonal preterite of kyscu 'sleep', the tale's discreet formula for a marriage made; genti 'with her' (gan, 3 sg. fem.; genthi above).

sentences.t: “Ar ny deryw o'r wled,” heb y Pryderi, “treulwch chwi, a minheu a af y hebrwng uy gwrogaeth y Gaswallawn uab Beli hyt yn Lloegyr.”
sentences.l: “What does-not end of the feast,” said Pryderi, “consume you, and I-for-my-part it-is-that will-go to convey my homage to Caswallon son of-Beli as-far-as into England.”
sentences.i: “Consume what remains of the feast,” said Pryderi, “and I will go and carry my homage to Caswallon son of Beli in England.”
sentences.n: Ar ny deryw o'r wled 'what does not come to an end of the feast': ar 'that which' (the article with the relative), and deryw, the 3 sg. present-perfect of daruot 'be finished'. treulwch 'consume, spend', 2 pl. imperative of treulaw. minheu a af 'I for my part will go'. y hebrwng 'to convey': hebrwng 'escort, bring'. gwrogaeth 'homage', which a man (gwr) does to his lord. y Gaswallawn 'to Caswallon' ← Caswallawn, softened after y 'to'; uab ← mab. Lloegyr is England (Lloegr).

sentences.t: “Arglwyd,” heb y Riannon, “yg Kent y mae Caswallawn, a thi a elly treulaw y wled honn, a'y arhos a uo nes.”
sentences.l: “Lord,” said Rhiannon, “in Kent it-is-that is Caswallon, and you it-is-that can spend this feast, and his awaiting while-he-may-be nearer.”
sentences.i: “Lord,” said Rhiannon, “Caswallon is in Kent; you can well finish this feast, and wait for him until he is nearer.”
sentences.n: yg Kent 'in Kent': yn with nasal mutation before k, written yg K, as yg Kymry. y mae Caswallawn: the place first, then y mae 'is'. a thi a elly 'and you can': ti with the spirant after a; elly ← gelly, 2 sg. present of gallu, softened. y wled honn 'this feast'. a'y arhos 'and his waiting' = waiting for him: the object as a possessive. a uo nes 'that he be nearer': uo ← bo, the subjunctive of bot, softened; the clause stands loosely for 'until he is nearer'.

sentences.t: “Ninheu a'y arhown,” heb ef.
sentences.l: “We-for-our-part it-is-that will-wait-for-him,” said he.
sentences.i: “Then we will wait for him,” he said.
sentences.n: Ninheu 'we for our part'. a'y arhown 'will wait for him': 'y is the infixed object pronoun 'him', and arhown is the 1 pl. present of arhos.

sentences.t: A'r wled honno a dreulyssant, a dechreu a wnaethant kylchaw Dyuet, a'y hela, a chymryt eu digriuwch.
sentences.l: And that feast it-is-that they-consumed, and beginning they-did circuiting Dyfed, and its hunting, and taking their pleasure.
sentences.i: And they finished that feast, and began to make the round of Dyfed, and to hunt it, and to take their pleasure.
sentences.n: A'r wled honno a dreulyssant: the object first, then a and the verb: treulyssant, 3 pl. preterite in -yssant, softened. dechreu a wnaethant 'beginning they did' = they began, with three verbal nouns depending on it. kylchaw 'go round', the lord's circuit of his land. a'y hela 'and its hunting', the object as a possessive. digriuwch 'pleasure' (house).

sentences.t: Ac wrth rodyaw y wlat ny welsynt eiryoet wlat gyuanhedach no hi, na heldir well, nac amlach y mel na'y physcawt no hi.
sentences.l: And while wandering the land they-had-not-seen ever a land more-settled than it, nor hunting-land better, nor more-plentiful its honey and its fish than it.
sentences.i: And as they went about the land, they had never seen a land better peopled, nor better hunting-ground, nor one more plentiful in honey and in fish.
sentences.n: wrth rodyaw 'in roaming' = while they roamed: wrth with a verbal noun. ny welsynt 'they had not seen': gwelsynt, 3 pl. pluperfect, softened after ny. gyuanhedach ← kyuanhedach, comparative of kyuanhed 'inhabited, settled', softened after the feminine wlat. heldir 'hunting land' (hela + tir). amlach 'more plentiful'. y mel na'y physcawt 'its honey nor its fish': y 'its' (for the feminine gwlat) gives the spirant, pyscawt > physcawt. no hi 'than it'.

sentences.t: Ac yn hynny tyuu kedymdeithas y rydunt yll pedwar, hyt na mynnei yr un uot heb y gilid na dyd na nos.
sentences.l: And in that grew fellowship between-them the-four-of-them, so-that did-not-want the one to-be without the other neither day nor night.
sentences.i: And meanwhile such fellowship grew among the four of them that none would be without the others, day or night.
sentences.n: Ac yn hynny 'and in that', meanwhile. tyuu 'grew', 3 sg. preterite of tyuu (tyfu). kedymdeithas 'fellowship' (house). y rydunt 'between them' (rwng, 3 pl.). yll pedwar 'the four of them'. hyt na 'so that not'. mynnei, imperfect of mynnu. uot ← bot, softened as the object. y gilid 'the other'.

sentences.t: Ac ymysc hynny, ef a aeth at Caswallawn hyt yn Ryt Ychen y hebrwng y wrogaeth idaw.
sentences.l: And amidst that, he it-is-that went to Caswallon as-far-as to Ryt Ychen to convey his homage to-him.
sentences.i: And in the meantime he went to Caswallon at Oxford to carry his homage to him.
sentences.n: ymysc hynny 'amidst that', meanwhile. ef a aeth 'he went': aeth, 3 sg. preterite of mynet; ef is Pryderi. Ryt Ychen 'the ford of oxen', the Welsh name of Oxford, written as two words as Evans prints it. y wrogaeth ← gwrogaeth, softened after y 'his'. idaw 'to him'.

sentences.t: A diruawr lywenyd a uu yn y erbyn yno, a diolwch idaw hebrwng y wrogaeth idaw.
sentences.l: And huge joy it-is-that was against-him there, and thanking to-him conveying his homage to-him.
sentences.i: And there was great rejoicing to meet him there, and he was thanked for bringing his homage.
sentences.n: diruawr lywenyd 'huge joy': llywenyd softened after diruawr. a uu 'was', 3 sg. preterite of bot. yn y erbyn 'to meet him': yn erbyn 'against, to meet', with y 'his' between. diolwch idaw hebrwng 'thanking him (for) bringing': the thing thanked for follows with no preposition.

sentences.t: A guedy ymchwelut, kymryt eu gwledeu ac eu hesmwythder a orugant Pryderi a Manawydan.
sentences.l: And after returning, taking their feasts and their ease they-did Pryderi and Manawydan.
sentences.i: And when he had come back, Pryderi and Manawydan took their feasting and their ease.
sentences.n: guedy ymchwelut 'after returning'. kymryt … a orugant 'taking they did': orugant is the 3 pl. of oruc, the preterite of gwneuthur, with the subject named after it. gwledeu 'feasts', plural of gwled. eu hesmwythder 'their ease': eu 'their' puts h before a vowel (esmwythder).

sentences.t: A dechreu gwled a orugant yn Arberth, canys prif lys oed, ac o honei y dechreuit pob anryded.
sentences.l: And beginning a feast they-did in Arberth, since chief court it-was, and from it was-begun every rank.
sentences.i: And they began a feast at Arberth, since it was the chief court, and from it all rank had its beginning.
sentences.n: canys 'since, for'. prif lys 'chief court': prif stands before its noun and softens it (llys > lys). o honei 'from it' (o, 3 sg. fem.; llys is feminine here). y dechreuit 'was begun': dechreuit, the impersonal imperfect in -it of dechreu. anryded 'rank' (house): the court is the source of every dignity and ceremony of the realm.

sentences.t: A guedy y bwyta kyntaf y nos honno, tra uei y gwassanaethwyr yn bwyta, kyuodi allan a orugant, a chyrchu Gorssed Arberth a wnaethant yll pedwar, ac yniuer gyt ac wynt.
sentences.l: And after the first eating that night, while were the servants eating, rising out they-did, and making-for the Mound of-Arberth they-did the-four-of-them, and the company with them.
sentences.i: And after the first sitting at table that night, while the servants were eating, they rose and went out, and the four of them made for the Mound of Arberth, and their company with them.
sentences.n: y bwyta kyntaf 'the first eating', the first sitting of the feast, as in the First Branch. tra uei 'while (they) were': uei ← bei, imperfect subjunctive of bot, softened after tra; singular before the plural noun. kyuodi allan a orugant 'rising out they did'. Gorssed Arberth is the Mound of Arberth, where Pwyll first saw Rhiannon. yniuer is y niuer 'the company', written together (yniueroed in the First Branch). gyt ac wynt 'with them'.

sentences.t: Ac ual y bydant yn eisted yuelly, llyma dwrwf, a chan ueint y twrwf, llyma gawat o nywl yn dyuot, hyt na chanhoed yr un ohonunt wy y gilid.
sentences.l: And as they-are sitting thus, behold a noise, and with the size of-the noise, behold a shower of mist coming, so-that did-not-see the one of-them the other.
sentences.i: And as they sat so, there came a great noise, and with the force of the noise a shower of mist came down, so that not one of them could see another.
sentences.n: ual y bydant 'as they are': the vivid present of bot in past narrative. yuelly 'thus' (felly). llyma 'behold, here is' throws the scene before the reader's eyes, and softens what follows: dwrwf ← twrwf 'noise', gawat ← kawat 'shower'. a chan ueint 'and with the size': can 'with' with the spirant after a, and meint softened after can. nywl 'mist'. na chanhoed 'did not see': kanhoed, imperfect of kanuot 'perceive', with the spirant after na. yr un ohonunt wy y gilid 'the one of them the other'.

sentences.t: Ac yn ol y nywl, llyma yn goleuhau pob lle.
sentences.l: And after the mist, behold growing-light every place.
sentences.i: And after the mist, every place grew bright.
sentences.n: yn ol 'after', as in yn ol y twrwf in the First Branch. llyma again. goleuhau 'grow light' (goleu 'light' + -hau), the verbal noun with yn.

sentences.t: A phan edrychyssant y ford y guelyn y preideu a'r anreitheu a'r kyuanhed kyn no hynny, ny welynt neb ryw dim, na thy, nac aniueil, na mwc, na than, na dyn, na chyuanhed, eithyr tei y llys yn wac, diffeith, anghyuanhed, heb dyn, heb uil yndi;
sentences.l: And when they-looked the way that they-used-to-see the flocks and the herds and the dwellings before than that, they-did-not-see any kind of thing, neither house, nor beast, nor smoke, nor fire, nor man, nor dwelling, except the houses of-the court empty, desolate, uninhabited, without man, without beast in-it;
sentences.i: And when they looked where before they had been used to see the flocks and the herds and the dwellings, they saw nothing of any kind: no house, no beast, no smoke, no fire, no man, no dwelling; only the buildings of the court, empty, desolate, uninhabited, with neither man nor beast in it;
sentences.n: edrychyssant 'they looked', 3 pl. preterite in -yssant. y ford y 'the way that' = where (ford is ffordd). y guelyn 'that they used to see': imperfect of gwelet, as welynt later in the sentence, here without the final t. preideu 'herds, flocks' and anreitheu 'herds, spoils' (preid, anreith); kyuanhed 'habitation'. kyn no hynny 'before that'. neb ryw dim 'any kind of thing'. na thy, na than: ty 'house' and tan 'fire' with the spirant after na. tei 'houses', plural of ty. yn wac ← gwac 'empty', softened after yn. anghyuanhed 'uninhabited' (an- 'un-', nasal before k). heb uil 'without beast': mil 'animal' softened after heb. yndi 'in it', 3 sg. fem., referring to the llys: the White Book's reading (Evans yndi); the second witness and the Red Book have yndunt 'in them', referring to the tei.

sentences.t: eu kedymdeithon e hun wedy eu colli, heb wybot dim y wrthunt, onyt wyll pedwar.
sentences.l: their companions themselves after their losing, without knowing anything about-them, except they the-four-of-them.
sentences.i: their own companions lost, and nothing known of them; there were only the four of them.
sentences.n: eu kedymdeithon e hun 'their own companions': e hun 'self, own' (ehun). wedy eu colli 'after their losing' = lost. heb wybot 'without knowing': gwybot softened after heb. y wrthunt 'about them' (y wrth, 3 pl.). onyt 'except'. wyll pedwar: so the White Book (Evans wyll), a run-together writing of wy yll pedwar 'they, the four of them'; the Red Book has hwy yll pedwar. Kept as written.

sentences.t: “Oy a Arglwyd Duw,” heb y Manawydan, “mae yniuer y llys, ac yn anniuer ninheu, namyn hynn? Awn y edrych.”
sentences.l: “Oh Lord God,” said Manawydan, “where-is the company of-the court, and our company ourselves, but this? Let-us-go to look.”
sentences.i: “Oh Lord God,” said Manawydan, “where is the company of the court, and our own company, all but ourselves? Let us go and look.”
sentences.n: mae 'where is', the interrogative (not y mae 'is'). yniuer y llys 'the company of the court'. yn anniuer ninheu 'our own company': yn here is an 'our' (the Red Book has an niuer), and the doubled n is an + niuer; ninheu 'we ourselves' strengthens the possessive. namyn hynn 'except this', apart from the four of them. Awn 'let us go', 1 pl. imperative of mynet. y edrych 'to look'.

sentences.t: Dyuot y'r yneuad a wnaethant; nit oed neb.
sentences.l: Coming to the hall they-did; there-was-not anyone.
sentences.i: They came into the hall; there was no one.
sentences.n: Dyuot … a wnaethant 'coming they did'. y'r yneuad 'to the hall': y 'to' + yr 'the'. nit oed neb 'there was not anyone'.

sentences.t: Kyrchu yr ystauell a'r hundy; ny welynt neb.
sentences.l: Making-for the chamber and the sleeping-house; they-did-not-see anyone.
sentences.i: They made for the chamber and the sleeping-house; they saw no one.
sentences.n: Kyrchu 'making for', the bare verbal noun with no a wnaethant, carrying on from the last sentence. ystauell 'chamber', the private room; hundy 'sleeping-house' (hun 'sleep' + ty). ny welynt 'they did not see': gwelynt, 3 pl. imperfect, softened.

sentences.t: Ymedgell, nac yg kegin, nit oed namyn diffeithwch.
sentences.l: In-the-mead-cellar, nor in the kitchen, there-was-not but desolation.
sentences.i: In the mead-cellar and in the kitchen there was nothing but desolation.
sentences.n: Ymedgell is ym medgell 'in the mead-cellar' (med 'mead' + kell 'cell'): yn becomes ym before m, and the doubled m is written once, with the whole as one word (Evans Ymedgell; the Red Book ym medgell). It is left undivided, since dividing it would need a letter the page does not have. nac yg kegin 'nor in the kitchen': yn + kegin with the nasal, written yg k; nac 'nor' implies a neither before it. diffeithwch 'desolation'.

sentences.t: Dechreu a wnaethant yll pedwar treulaw y wled, a hela a wnaethant, a chymryt eu digriuwch; a dechreu a wnaeth pob un o honunt rodyaw y wlat a'r kyuoeth y edrych a welynt ay ty ay kyuanhed; a neb ryw dim ny welynt eithyr guydlwdyn.
sentences.l: Beginning they-did the-four-of-them consuming the feast, and hunting they-did, and taking their pleasure; and beginning did every one of-them roaming the land and the realm to see whether they-saw either house or dwelling; and any kind of thing they-did-not-see except wild-beasts.
sentences.i: The four of them began to eat their way through the feast, and they hunted, and took their pleasure; and each of them began to roam the land and the realm to see whether they could find any house or dwelling; and they saw nothing of any kind but wild beasts.
sentences.n: Dechreu a wnaethant yll pedwar treulaw 'beginning the four of them did, consuming': the subject sits between a wnaethant and the verbal noun it governs. pob un o honunt 'every one of them'. y edrych a welynt 'to see whether they saw': a 'whether'. ay … ay 'either … or'. a neb ryw dim ny welynt 'and any kind of thing they did not see': the object first. guydlwdyn 'wild beast' (gwyd 'wild' + llwdyn 'beast', ll softened in the compound), a collective singular.

sentences.t: A guedy treulaw eu gwled ac eu darmerth o honunt, dechreu a wnaethant ymborth ar kic hela, a physcawt, a bydaueu.
sentences.l: And after consuming their feast and their provision by-them, beginning they-did feeding on flesh of-hunting, and fish, and wild-swarms.
sentences.i: And when they had used up their feast and their provisions, they began to live on game, and fish, and the honey of wild swarms.
sentences.n: guedy treulaw … o honunt 'after consuming … by them': o marks the doers of a verbal noun. darmerth 'provision, store'. ymborth ar 'feed on, live on'. ar kic hela 'on flesh of hunting', game; after ar one expects gic, and the mutation is not written. a physcawt: pyscawt 'fish' with the spirant after a. bydaueu, plural of bydaf 'wild swarm, wild bees' nest'.

sentences.t: Ac yuelly blwydyn a'r eil a dreulyssant yn digrif gantunt.
sentences.l: And thus a year and the second they-spent pleasantly with-them.
sentences.i: And so they spent a year, and a second, to their liking.
sentences.n: yuelly 'thus'. blwydyn a'r eil 'a year and the second', a second year. a dreulyssant 'they spent', the object first. yn digrif gantunt 'pleasant with them', to their liking: digrif after yn is softened, but d shows nothing (d also writes dd). gantunt 'with them' (gan, 3 pl.).

sentences.t: Ac yn y diwed, dygyaw a wnaethant.
sentences.l: And in the end, growing-weary they-did.
sentences.i: And in the end they grew weary of it.
sentences.n: yn y diwed 'in the end'. dygyaw a wnaethant 'dygyaw they did': the verb is rare and its meaning uncertain; it seems to mean 'have had enough, grow weary, be sated', and its preterite dygywys below ('until it became too much for their fellow-townsmen') fits the same sense.

sentences.t: “Dioer,” heb y Manawydan, “ny bydwn ual hynn. Kyrchwn Loygyr, a cheisswn greft y caffom yn ymborth.”
sentences.l: “Indeed,” said Manawydan, “we-will-not-be like this. Let-us-make-for England, and let-us-seek a craft that we-may-get our sustenance.”
sentences.i: “Indeed,” said Manawydan, “we will not go on like this. Let us make for England and look for a craft by which we may earn our keep.”
sentences.n: Dioer 'indeed, surely'. ny bydwn 'we will not be', 1 pl. of bot. ual hynn 'like this'. Kyrchwn, a cheisswn 'let us make for, and let us seek': 1 pl. imperatives, keisswn with the spirant after a. Loygyr ← Lloygyr, another spelling of Lloegr, softened as the object. greft ← kreft 'craft'. y caffom 'that we may get': caffom, 1 pl. present subjunctive of caffael, with ff as Evans prints it. yn ymborth 'our sustenance': yn is an 'our', as yn anniuer above.

sentences.t: Kyrchu Lloygyr a orugant, a dyuot hyt yn Henford, a chymryt arnunt gwneuthur kyfrwyeu.
sentences.l: Making-for England they-did, and coming as-far-as to Hereford, and taking on-them making saddles.
sentences.i: They made for England, and came as far as Hereford, and set up as makers of saddles.
sentences.n: Kyrchu … a orugant 'making for they did'. Henford is Hereford (Welsh Henffordd, 'old road', f for ff). kymryt arnunt 'taking upon them', to undertake, profess a trade. kyfrwyeu 'saddles', plural of kyfrwy.

sentences.t: A dechreu a wnaeth ef Uanawydan llunyaw corueu, ac eu lliwaw ar y wed y guelsei gan Lassar Llaes Gygnwyt, a chalch llassar, a gwneuthur calch lassar racdaw, ual y gwnathoed y gwr arall.
sentences.l: And beginning did he Manawydan shaping saddle-bows, and their colouring in the manner that he-had-seen with Llasar Llaes Gygnwyd, and calch llassar, and making calch lassar before-him, as had-done the other man.
sentences.i: And Manawydan began to shape saddle-bows and colour them in the way he had seen Llasar Llaes Gyfnewid do, with calch llasar, the blue enamel; and he went on to make calch llasar himself, as the other man had done.
sentences.n: ef Uanawydan 'he, Manawydan': the pronoun, then the name softened in apposition (as heb ef Pryderi above). llunyaw 'shape'. corueu, plural of corf 'saddle-bow'. eu lliwaw 'their colouring' = colouring them. ar y wed 'in the manner' (gwed softened after the article). y guelsei 'that he had seen', pluperfect. gan Lassar ← Llassar, softened after gan. Llassar Llaes Gygnwyt is the Llasar Llaes Gyfnewid of the Second Branch, who brought the cauldron out of the lake; the epithet is spelt differently in each place, and English keeps the form used where he first appears. calch llassar: calch is 'lime, plaster', and also the coating or enamel of a shield or saddle-bow; llassar seems to mean 'azure, blue enamel'. What exactly the stuff was is uncertain, and English keeps the Welsh name, since the next sentence explains it. The White Book writes calch llassar and calch lassar side by side. racdaw 'before him', onward. gwnathoed 'had done', the pluperfect of gwneuthur.

sentences.t: Ac wrth hynny y gelwir etwa calch llassar, am y wneuthur o Lassar Llaes Gygnwyt.
sentences.l: And by that is-called still calch llassar, because-of its making by Llasar Llaes Gygnwyd.
sentences.i: And that is why it is still called calch llasar: because Llasar Llaes Gyfnewid made it.
sentences.n: wrth hynny 'by that', for that reason. y gelwir 'it is called': gelwir, the impersonal present of galw, softened after the particle. etwa 'still'. am y wneuthur o Lassar 'for its making by Llasar': gwneuthur softened after y 'its', and o marking the doer, softening Llassar. The tale explains a word by a person, as it explains names of places.

sentences.t: Ac o'r gueith hwnnw, tra geffit gan Uanawydan, ny phrynit gan gyfrwyd dros wyneb Henford na choryf na chyfrwy, yny adnabu pob un o'r kyfrwydyon y uot yn colli o'y henill, ac ny frynit dim ganthunt onyt guedy na cheffit gan Uanawydan.
sentences.l: And of that work, while was-got from Manawydan, there-was-not-bought from a saddler over the face of-Hereford neither saddle-bow nor saddle, until knew every one of the saddlers that he-was losing of his gain, and there-was-not-bought anything from-them except after there-was-not-got from Manawydan.
sentences.i: And of that work, so long as any could be had from Manawydan, not a saddle-bow nor a saddle was bought from any saddler in all Hereford, until every one of the saddlers knew that he was losing his earnings, and nothing was bought from them except when none could be had from Manawydan.
sentences.n: tra geffit 'while (any) was got': keffit, the impersonal imperfect of caffael, softened after tra. ny phrynit 'there was not bought': prynit, impersonal imperfect of prynu, with the spirant after ny; the r is written above the line in the manuscript and is brought into it here. gan gyfrwyd ← kyfrwyd 'saddler', softened after gan; kyfrwydyon is its plural. dros wyneb 'over the face of', throughout. na choryf na chyfrwy: koryf (another spelling of corf) and kyfrwy with the spirant after na. yny 'until'. adnabu 'knew', preterite of adnabot. y uot 'his being' = that he was. o'y henill 'of his gain': 'y puts h before a vowel. ny frynit has the soft mutation (f = v) after ny where the sentence opened with the spirant: both are found. onyt guedy 'except after'.

sentences.t: Ac yn hyny, ymgynullaw y gyt ohonunt, a duunaw ar y lad ef a'y gedymdeith.
sentences.l: And in that, gathering together by-them, and agreeing on his killing him and his companion.
sentences.i: And at that they gathered together and agreed to kill him and his companion.
sentences.n: Ac yn hyny: hyny is the White Book's spelling of hynny (Evans prints a suspension stroke over the n, dropped here as elsewhere). ymgynullaw 'assemble' (ym- reflexive), and the doers marked by ohonunt 'by them'. duunaw ar 'agree on' (du- + un 'one': become one). y lad ef 'his killing' = to kill him: llad softened after y 'his', with ef closing. a'y gedymdeith 'and his companion' ← kedymdeith.

sentences.t: Ac yn hynny rybud a gawssont wynteu, a chymryt kynghor am adaw y dref.
sentences.l: And in that warning they-got they-for-their-part, and taking counsel about leaving the town.
sentences.i: And meanwhile they had warning of it, and took counsel about leaving the town.
sentences.n: rybud 'warning', the object first. a gawssont ← kawssont, 3 pl. preterite of caffael, softened. wynteu 'they for their part'. am adaw 'about leaving'.

sentences.t: “E rof i a Duw,” heb y Pryderi, “ni chynghoraf i adaw y dref, namyn llad y tayogeu racco.”
sentences.l: “Between me and God,” said Pryderi, “I-do-not-advise leaving the town, but killing the churls yonder.”
sentences.i: “Between me and God,” said Pryderi, “I do not advise leaving the town, but killing those churls over there.”
sentences.n: E rof i a Duw 'between me and God' (house): y rof 'between me' (rwng, 1 sg.), with e for y. ni chynghoraf 'I do not advise': kynghoraf with the spirant after ni. namyn 'but'. tayogeu 'churls', plural of tayawc, a man of the unfree class, used in contempt. racco 'yonder, over there'.

sentences.t: “Nac ef,” heb y Manawydan, “bei ymladem ni ac wyntwy, clot drwc uydei arnam, ac yn carcharu a wneit. Ys guell in,” heb ef, “kyrchu tref arall e ymossymdeithaw yndi.”
sentences.l: “No,” said Manawydan, “if we-fought we with them, ill fame would-be on-us, and our imprisoning would-be-done. It-is better for-us,” said he, “making-for another town to get-our-living in-it.”
sentences.i: “No,” said Manawydan; “if we fought with them, we should have an ill name, and we should be put in prison. It is better for us,” he said, “to make for another town and earn our living there.”
sentences.n: Nac ef 'not it' = no. bei ymladem 'if we fought': bei 'if' with ymladem, 1 pl. imperfect subjunctive. wyntwy 'them', the doubled pronoun. clot drwc 'ill fame'. uydei ← bydei 'would be', conditional of bot, softened. arnam 'on us' (ar, 1 pl.). yn carcharu a wneit 'our imprisoning would be done': yn is an 'our', and wneit the impersonal imperfect of gwneuthur. Ys guell in 'it is better for us': ys 'is', an old form; in 'to us'. e ymossymdeithaw 'to get our living': e is y 'to'; ymossymdeithaw is a rare verb, apparently 'maintain oneself, make a livelihood' (from ossymdeith 'sustenance'). yndi 'in it' (tref is feminine).

sentences.t: Ac yna kyrchu dinas arall a wnaethant yll pedwar.
sentences.l: And then making-for another city they-did the-four-of-them.
sentences.i: And then the four of them made for another city.
sentences.n: kyrchu … a wnaethant yll pedwar, as before. dinas 'city', a walled town.

sentences.t: “Pa geluydyt,” heb y Pryderi, “a gymerwn ni arnam?”
sentences.l: “What craft,” said Pryderi, “shall-we-take we on-us?”
sentences.i: “What craft,” said Pryderi, “shall we take up?”
sentences.n: Pa geluydyt 'what craft' ← keluydyt, softened after pa. a gymerwn 'shall we take': kymerwn, 1 pl. present of kymryt, softened after a. arnam 'on us', to take on.

sentences.t: “Gwnawn taryaneu,” heb y Manawydan.
sentences.l: “Let-us-make shields,” said Manawydan.
sentences.i: “Let us make shields,” said Manawydan.
sentences.n: Gwnawn 'let us make', 1 pl. imperative of gwneuthur. taryaneu 'shields', plural of taryan; the object after the imperative is here left unsoftened.

sentences.t: “A wdom ninheu dim y wrth hynny?” heb y Pryderi.
sentences.l: “Do-we-know we-for-our-part anything about that?” said Pryderi.
sentences.i: “Do we know anything about that?” said Pryderi.
sentences.n: A wdom 'do we know': the question particle a with gwdom, 1 pl. present of gwybot, softened. ninheu 'we for our part'. y wrth 'about'.

sentences.t: “Ni a'y prouwn,” heb ynteu.
sentences.l: “We it-is-that will-try-it,” said he-for-his-part.
sentences.i: “We will try it,” he said.
sentences.n: Ni a'y prouwn 'we will try it': 'y the infixed object 'it', and prouwn, 1 pl. present of prouaf 'try, test' (profi).

sentences.t: Dechreu gwneuthur gueith y taryaneu, eu llunyaw ar weith taryaneu da welsynt, a dodi y lliw a dodyssynt ar y kyfrwyeu arnunt.
sentences.l: Beginning making the work of-the shields, their shaping on the work of good shields they-had-seen, and putting the colour that they-had-put on the saddles on-them.
sentences.i: They set to the work of the shields, shaping them on the pattern of good shields they had seen, and putting on them the colour they had put on the saddles.
sentences.n: Dechreu gwneuthur 'beginning making': the bare verbal noun chain. eu llunyaw 'their shaping' = shaping them. ar weith 'on the work of', after the fashion of: gweith softened after ar. taryaneu da welsynt 'good shields (that) they had seen': the relative a is not written before welsynt (so Evans, and the second witness), though the softened verb implies it. dodyssynt 'they had put', 3 pl. pluperfect of dodi. arnunt 'on them' (ar, 3 pl.).

sentences.t: A'r gweith hwnnw a lwydwys racdunt, hyt na phrynit taryan yn yr holl dref onyt guedy na cheffit ganthunt wy.
sentences.l: And that work it-is-that prospered before-them, so-that there-was-not-bought a shield in the whole town except after there-was-not-got from-them.
sentences.i: And that work prospered for them, so that not a shield was bought in all the town except when none was to be had from them.
sentences.n: a lwydwys 'prospered': llwydwys, 3 sg. preterite in -wys of llwydaw, softened after a. racdunt 'before them', for them. na phrynit, as with the saddles: the same pattern, the same words. yn yr holl dref 'in the whole town': holl stands before its noun and softens it. ganthunt wy 'from them'.

sentences.t: Kyflym oed y gueith wynteu, a diuessur a wneynt; ac yuelly y buant yny dygywys y'w kytdrefwyr racdunt, ac yny duunyssant ar geissaw eu llad.
sentences.l: Swift was their work, and measureless they-made; and thus they-were until it-galled to their fellow-townsmen because-of-them, and until they-agreed on seeking their killing.
sentences.i: Their work was quick, and they made it beyond all measure; and so they went on until their fellow-townsmen had had enough of them, and agreed to seek to kill them.
sentences.n: Kyflym oed 'swift was', the predicate first. y gueith wynteu 'their work': y here stands for 'their', with wynteu. diuessur a wneynt 'measureless they made': diuessur is di- 'without' + messur 'measure', and whether it means that they made shields in great numbers or past measuring for quality is uncertain. wneynt ← gwneynt, 3 pl. imperfect. yny dygywys 'until it became too much': dygywys, 3 sg. preterite of the uncertain dygyaw (see above). y'w kytdrefwyr 'to their fellow-townsmen': y'w is y 'to' + 'w 'their'; kyt- 'fellow' + tref + gwyr. duunyssant 'they agreed', 3 pl. preterite. ar geissaw ← keissaw 'seek', softened after ar.

sentences.t: Rybud a doeth udunt wynteu, a chlybot bot y gwyr ac y bryt ar eu dienydyaw.
sentences.l: Warning it-is-that came to-them they-for-their-part, and hearing that the men were and their mind on their putting-to-death.
sentences.i: Word of it came to them, and they heard that the men had set their minds on putting them to death.
sentences.n: a doeth 'came', 3 sg. preterite of dyuot. a chlybot 'and hearing': klybot with the spirant after a. bot y gwyr ac y bryt ar 'that the men were, and their mind on': bryt 'mind, intent' with y standing for their (or a collective 'his'); the men were set upon it. dienydyaw 'put to death'.

sentences.t: “Pryderi,” heb y Manawydan, “y mae y gwyr hynn yn mynnu yn diuetha.”
sentences.l: “Pryderi,” said Manawydan, “these men are wanting our destroying.”
sentences.i: “Pryderi,” said Manawydan, “these men mean to destroy us.”
sentences.n: y mae y gwyr hynn 'these men are': the plain order, particle y + mae + subject. yn mynnu 'wanting'. yn diuetha 'our destroying': yn for an 'our' again; diuetha 'destroy'.

sentences.t: “Ny chymerwn inheu y gan y tayogeu hynny. Awn adanunt a lladwn.”
sentences.l: “We-will-not-take we-for-our-part from those churls. Let-us-go at-them and let-us-kill.”
sentences.i: “We will not take it from those churls. Let us go at them and kill them.”
sentences.n: Pryderi's answer, untagged. Ny chymerwn 'we will not take': kymerwn, 1 pl., with the spirant after ny. The verb has no expressed object ('take [it]'); the second witness marks a gap here, but the sense is complete and nothing is supplied. inheu is so written (Evans inheu); with a 1 pl. verb it stands for 'we for our part', as ninheu would (the witness's reading). y gan 'from'. adanunt 'at them', at conjugated, 3 pl. lladwn 'let us kill', 1 pl. imperative, object understood.

sentences.t: “Nac ef,” heb ynteu, “Casswallawn a glywei hynny, a'e wyr, a rewin uydem. Kyrchu tref arall a wnawn.”
sentences.l: “No,” said he-for-his-part, “Caswallon would-hear that, and his men, and ruined we-would-be. Making-for another town we-will-do.”
sentences.i: “No,” he said; “Caswallon would hear of it, and his men, and we should be ruined. We will make for another town.”
sentences.n: Casswallawn, here spelt with ss. a glywei 'would hear': klywei, imperfect of klywet, softened, with the conditional sense of the imperfect. a'e wyr 'and his men': 'e is y 'his', softening gwyr. a rewin uydem 'and ruin we would be': rewin 'ruin' (Latin ruina), the predicate first; uydem ← bydem, 1 pl. conditional of bot. Kyrchu … a wnawn 'making for we will do': wnawn, 1 pl. present of gwneuthur.

sentences.t: Vynt a doethant y dref arall.
sentences.l: They it-was-that came to another town.
sentences.i: They came to another town.
sentences.n: Vynt a doethant, as above. y dref arall 'to another town': tref softened after y 'to'. The scribe first wrote deef, then marked the e and wrote r above it, correcting it to dref, which is read.

sentences.t: “Pa geluydyt yd awni wrthi?” heb y Manawydan.
sentences.l: “What craft is-it-that we-go to-it?” said Manawydan.
sentences.i: “What craft shall we take to?” said Manawydan.
sentences.n: yd awni 'we go': yd, the particle before a vowel, with awn 'we go' (1 pl. present of mynet) and ni fused on. wrthi 'to it' (wrth, 3 sg. fem., for keluydyt).

sentences.t: “Yr honn y mynnych, o'r a wdam,” heb y Pryderi.
sentences.l: “The one that you-may-want, of what we-know,” said Pryderi.
sentences.i: “Whichever you please, of those we know,” said Pryderi.
sentences.n: Yr honn 'the one' (feminine, for keluydyt). y mynnych 'that you may want': mynnych, 2 sg. present subjunctive of mynnu. o'r a wdam 'of what we know': o 'of' + yr 'the' + a relative; wdam is wdom spelt with a.

sentences.t: “Nac ef,” heb ynteu, “gwnawn grydyaeth. Ni byd o galhon gan grydyon nac ymlad a ni nac ymwarauun.”
sentences.l: “No,” said he-for-his-part, “let-us-make shoemaking. There-will-not-be of heart with shoemakers either fighting with us or forbidding.”
sentences.i: “No,” he said, “let us take up shoemaking. Shoemakers will not have the heart either to fight us or to stand in our way.”
sentences.n: Nac ef 'no': not any craft they know, but one they do not. gwnawn grydyaeth 'let us do shoemaking': krydyaeth softened as the object. Ni byd o galhon gan grydyon 'there will not be of galhon with shoemakers': galhon is taken as calon 'heart' (spelt with h) softened after o, 'they will not have the heart', but the reading is not certain. grydyon ← krydyon 'shoemakers', softened after gan. nac ymlad a ni nac ymwarauun 'either fighting with us or ymwarauun': ymwarauun seems to be ym- with gwarauun 'forbid, refuse, begrudge', so 'oppose, hinder'; the exact sense is uncertain.

sentences.t: “Ny wnn i dim y wrth honno,” heb y Pryderi.
sentences.l: “I-do-not-know anything about that,” said Pryderi.
sentences.i: “I know nothing about that,” said Pryderi.
sentences.n: Ny wnn 'I do not know': gwnn, 1 sg. present of gwybot, softened after ny. honno 'that' (feminine, for krydyaeth).

sentences.t: “Mi a'y gwn,” heb y Manawydan, “a mi a dyscaf it wniaw. Ac nit ymyrrwn ar gyweiraw lledyr, namyn y brynu yn barawt, a gwneuthur yn gueith ohonaw.”
sentences.l: “I it-is-that know-it,” said Manawydan, “and I it-is-that will-teach to-you sewing. And we-will-not-meddle with dressing leather, but its buying ready, and making into work of-it.”
sentences.i: “I know it,” said Manawydan, “and I will teach you to sew. And we will not meddle with dressing leather, but buy it ready-made and work it up.”
sentences.n: Mi a'y gwn 'I know it': 'y the infixed object. a mi a dyscaf it 'and I will teach you': dyscaf, 1 sg. present of dyscu. wniaw ← gwniaw 'sew', softened. nit ymyrrwn ar 'we will not meddle with': ymyrrwn, 1 pl. of ymyrru. gyweiraw ← kyweiraw 'prepare, dress', softened after ar. y brynu 'its buying' = buying it: prynu softened after y 'its'. yn barawt ← parawt 'ready'. gwneuthur yn gueith ohonaw 'making into work of it'.

sentences.t: Ac yna dechreu prynu y cordwal teccaf a gauas yn y dref; ac amgen ledyr no hwnnw ny phrynei ef, eithyr lledyr guadneu.
sentences.l: And then beginning buying the fairest cordovan that he-got in the town; and other leather than that he-would-not-buy, except leather of-soles.
sentences.i: And then he began to buy the finest cordovan to be had in the town; and no other leather than that would he buy, except leather for soles.
sentences.n: cordwal 'cordovan', the fine leather named from Córdoba. teccaf 'fairest', superlative of tec. a gauas 'that he got' ← kauas, 3 sg. preterite of caffael. amgen ledyr 'other leather': amgen stands before its noun and softens it (lledyr). ny phrynei 'he would not buy', imperfect with the spirant after ny. guadneu 'soles', plural of gwadn.

sentences.t: A dechreu a wnaeth ymgedymdeithassu a'r eurych goreu yn y dref, a pheri guaegeu y'r eskidyeu, ac euraw y guaegeu, a synnyaw e hun ar hynny yny gwybu.
sentences.l: And beginning he-did making-fellowship with the goldsmith best in the town, and causing buckles for the shoes, and gilding the buckles, and watching himself on that until he-knew.
sentences.i: And he made friends with the best goldsmith in the town, and had buckles made for the shoes, and the buckles gilded, and watched the work himself until he had learned it.
sentences.n: ymgedymdeithassu a 'make fellowship with'. eurych 'goldsmith', a worker in aur 'gold'. peri 'cause, have made'. guaegeu 'buckles', plural of gwaeg. eskidyeu 'shoes', plural of eskit. euraw 'gild'. synnyaw e hun ar hynny 'observing it himself': synnyaw 'mark, watch closely'. yny gwybu 'until he knew': gwybu, 3 sg. preterite of gwybot, here 'came to know'.

sentences.t: Ac o'r achaws hwnnw y gelwit ef yn tryded eurgryd.
sentences.l: And from that cause he-was-called the third gold-shoemaker.
sentences.i: And for that reason he was called the third Gold-Shoemaker.
sentences.n: y gelwit 'he was called': gelwit, the impersonal imperfect of galw, softened. yn tryded eurgryd 'the third gold-shoemaker', another triad (eurgryd: aur 'gold' + cryd 'shoemaker'). Two things are odd and the phrase is uncertain: tryded is the feminine form of 'third' (as in tryded anuat paluawt in the last part), though cryd is masculine; and after predicative yn one expects dryded.

sentences.t: Tra geffit gantaw ef nac eskit na hossan, ny phrynit dim gan gryd yn yr holl dref.
sentences.l: While was-got from-him either shoe or hose, there-was-not-bought anything from a shoemaker in the whole town.
sentences.i: So long as shoe or hose could be had from him, nothing was bought from any shoemaker in all the town.
sentences.n: The pattern of the saddlers and shield-makers once more. tra geffit, ny phrynit: impersonal imperfects of caffael and prynu. gantaw ef 'from him'. nac … na 'either … or', in a clause that leans on the negative to come. hossan 'hose', a leg-covering of leather or cloth. gan gryd ← kryd, softened after gan.

sentences.t: Sef a wnaeth y crydyon, adnabot bot eu hennill yn pallu udunt, canys ual y llunyei Uanawydan y gueith, y gwniei Pryderi.
sentences.l: That-is what did the shoemakers, knowing that their gain was failing to-them, since as shaped Manawydan the work, sewed Pryderi.
sentences.i: The shoemakers came to know that their earnings were failing them; for as fast as Manawydan cut out the work, Pryderi sewed it.
sentences.n: Sef a wnaeth y crydyon, adnabot 'that is what the shoemakers did: knowing'. eu hennill 'their gain': eu puts h before a vowel. pallu 'fail'. udunt 'to them'. ual y llunyei … y gwniei 'as he shaped … he sewed': imperfects of llunyaw and gwniaw. Uanawydan softened as the subject after the verb.

sentences.t: Dyuot y crydyon a chymryt kynghor; sef a gausant yn eu kynghor, duunaw ar eu llad.
sentences.l: Coming the shoemakers and taking counsel; that-is what they-got in their counsel, agreeing on their killing.
sentences.i: The shoemakers came together and took counsel; and what they came to in their counsel was to agree to kill them.
sentences.n: Dyuot … a chymryt 'coming … and taking', verbal nouns with the subject straight after. sef a gausant 'that is what they got': causant, 3 pl. preterite of caffael, softened. duunaw ar eu llad 'agreeing on their killing'.

sentences.t: “Pryderi,” heb y Manawydan, “y mae y guyr yn mynnu an llad.”
sentences.l: “Pryderi,” said Manawydan, “the men are wanting our killing.”
sentences.i: “Pryderi,” said Manawydan, “the men mean to kill us.”
sentences.n: y guyr 'the men', gwyr spelt gu-. an llad 'our killing': here 'our' is spelt an, as against yn diuetha and yn anniuer.

sentences.t: “Pam y kymerwn inheu hynny gan y tayogeu lladron,” heb y Pryderi, “namyn eu llad oll?”
sentences.l: “Why should-we-take we-for-our-part that from the churls thieves,” said Pryderi, “but their killing all?”
sentences.i: “Why should we take that from these thieving churls,” said Pryderi, “and not kill them all?”
sentences.n: Pam 'why'. y kymerwn 'should we take': kymerwn, 1 pl., after the particle y. inheu again for 'we for our part', where the second witness marks a gap; nothing is supplied, and hynny 'that' does duty as the object. tayogeu lladron 'churls thieves', two nouns side by side. namyn eu llad oll 'but (rather) killing them all'.

sentences.t: “Nac ef,” heb y Manawydan, “nyt ymladwn ac wynt, ac ny bydwn yn Lloygyr bellach. Kyrchwn parth a Dyuet, ac awn y hedrych.”
sentences.l: “No,” said Manawydan, “we-will-not-fight with them, and we-will-not-be in England further. Let-us-make-for towards Dyfed, and let-us-go to its seeing.”
sentences.i: “No,” said Manawydan, “we will not fight them, and we will stay in England no longer. Let us make for Dyfed, and go and see how it fares.”
sentences.n: nyt ymladwn ac wynt 'we will not fight with them': ymladwn, 1 pl. bellach 'any longer' (Evans bellach; the second witness ballach). Kyrchwn parth a Dyuet 'let us make towards Dyfed': parth a 'towards'. awn y hedrych 'let us go to its seeing' = to see it: y 'its' (Dyfed, feminine as a land) puts h before the vowel of edrych.
